# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by cli/tools/gen-reference.mjs from cli/commands/*.json and real sessions on the example labs.
     Do not edit by hand: change the command definitions or the tool, then run `node cli/tools/gen-reference.mjs`. -->

The OpenPacketRouter CLI is a console for one device at a time, the way you would plug a cable into the console
port of a real router or switch. You type commands, the device answers. It works the same on every device in a
lab: routers, switches, hosts and servers. Use the commands that fit the device (a switch has no `ip route`).

This page is for teachers and students. For the design, and for how to add a command, see
[docs/cli-design.md](cli-design.md) and [cli/README.md](../cli/README.md).

## Start a console

```bash
node cli/bin/opr-cli.mjs examples/routed-lan-dns/spec.json R1
```

The first word is the lab file, the second is the name of the device. Type `exit` to leave. In the Studio
(`npm run studio`) the same commands run in the console panel of each device.

To run commands without typing them, give each one with `-c`:

```bash
node cli/bin/opr-cli.mjs examples/routed-lan-dns/spec.json R1 -c enable -c "show ip route"
```

`--json` prints everything as one JSON list, which is easy to read from a script. `write` saves your changes
back into the lab file.

## Modes: where you are

The prompt tells you which mode you are in. Each mode allows different commands.

| Prompt | Mode | What you can do here | How to get here | How to leave |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `R1>` | user | Look around: most `show` commands, `ping`, `traceroute`. Nothing can be changed. | start | `exit` |
| `R1#` | privileged | Everything in user mode, plus `show running-config`, `write` and `configure terminal`. | `enable` | `disable` |
| `R1(config)#` | config | Change the device: its name, routes, DHCP and DNS settings. | `configure terminal` | `exit` or `end` |
| `R1(config-if)#` | interface | Change one interface or port: address, VLAN, shutdown. | `interface NAME` | `exit` (one step back) or `end` |
| `R1(config-dhcp)#` | DHCP pool | Change one DHCP address pool. | `ip dhcp pool NAME` | `exit` or `end` |

Anything that changes the device is checked first. If the new setting would not make a valid network, the
command is refused with a message starting with `%`, and the old setting stays.

## Typing less

- **Abbreviate.** Any unique start of a word works: `sh ip ro` means `show ip route`, `conf t` means `configure terminal`.
- **Ask `?`.** Type `?` where you are stuck to see what can come next, for example `show ip ?`.
- **Tab** completes the word you started.
- **`no`** in front of a configuration command undoes it: `no shutdown`, `no ip route …`.
- **`do`** runs a privileged command from inside a configuration mode: `do show running-config`.

## Filters: `| json`, `| include`, `| exclude`

Every `show` command can be followed by a pipe:

| Add | Result |
|---|---|
| `| json` | The same information as JSON: for scripts, spreadsheets and other programs. |
| `| include WORD` | Only the lines that contain WORD. |
| `| exclude WORD` | Only the lines that do not contain WORD. |

Lab `routed-lan-dns`, device `R1`:

```text
R1>enable
R1#show ip route
Legend: C = connected network, S = static route

C  10.0.0.0/24 on eth0 (directly connected)
C  10.1.0.0/24 on eth1 (directly connected)
R1#show ip route | include eth1
C  10.1.0.0/24 on eth1 (directly connected)
R1#show ip route | json
[
  {
    "prefix": "10.0.0.0/24",
    "protocol": "connected",
    "interface": "eth0"
  },
  {
    "prefix": "10.1.0.0/24",
    "protocol": "connected",
    "interface": "eth1"
  }
]
```

## All commands

Each table lists what to type, the mode it works in, which devices have it, and what it does. Words in
CAPITALS are things you fill in (for example `ADDRESS` is an IP address like `10.1.0.53`).

### Base

Moving between modes, the device name, saving.

| Command | Mode | Devices | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enable` | user | all devices | Go to privileged mode (configuration and every show command) |
| `disable` | privileged | all devices | Go back to user mode |
| `configure terminal` | privileged | all devices | Type the changes here, one command per line |
| `exit` | user, privileged, config, interface, routing, vlan, DHCP pool | all devices | Leave this mode (in user or privileged mode: close the session) |
| `end` | config, interface, routing, vlan, DHCP pool | all devices | Finish configuring and go back to privileged mode |
| `write` | privileged | all devices | Save the configuration |
| `write memory` | privileged | all devices | Save it where it is loaded from at start |
| `hostname NAME` | config | all devices | New name (letters, digits, - and _) |

### Interfaces

Selecting an interface; turning it off and on; addresses; shaping.

| Command | Mode | Devices | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `interface IFNAME` | config | all devices | Interface name |
| `shutdown` | interface | all devices | Turn this interface off |
| `no shutdown` | interface | all devices | Turn this interface back on |
| `description TEXT` | interface | all devices | The note |
| `no description` | interface | all devices | Remove the note |
| `ip address PREFIX` | interface | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Address and prefix length, like 10.0.0.1/24 |
| `ip address ADDRESS MASK` | interface | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Network mask, like 255.255.255.0 |
| `ip address dhcp` | interface | routers, hosts, servers | Ask a DHCP server for an address |
| `no ip address` | interface | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Remove the interface's address |
| `shape rate RATE burst BYTES limit QUEUE` | interface | all devices | Bytes |
| `no shape` | interface | all devices | Send at full speed again |

### Ip-routing

Static routes in FRRouting's style (ip route PREFIX NEXTHOP); the mask form and ip default-gateway are accepted too.

| Command | Mode | Devices | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip route PREFIX NEXTHOP` | config | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Address of the next router |
| `ip route NETWORK MASK NEXTHOP` | config | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Address of the next router |
| `no ip route PREFIX NEXTHOP` | config | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Remove a static route |
| `no ip route PREFIX` | config | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Remove a static route |
| `no ip route NETWORK MASK NEXTHOP` | config | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Remove a static route |
| `ip default-gateway GATEWAY` | config | routers, hosts, servers | Router address |
| `no ip default-gateway` | config | routers, hosts, servers | Remove the default route |

### Switching

Access and trunk ports, spanning tree. Common industry syntax.

| Command | Mode | Devices | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `switchport mode access` | interface | switches | Carry one VLAN, untagged |
| `switchport mode trunk` | interface | switches | Carry several VLANs, tagged |
| `switchport access vlan VLAN` | interface | switches | VLAN number |
| `switchport trunk allowed vlan VLANS` | interface | switches | VLANs, like 10,20,30-35 |
| `switchport trunk native vlan VLAN` | interface | switches | VLAN number |
| `no switchport access vlan` | interface | switches | Put the port back in VLAN 1 |
| `no switchport trunk native vlan` | interface | switches | Use the default native VLAN again |
| `no switchport mode` | interface | switches | Forget this port's VLAN settings |
| `spanning-tree` | config | switches | Spanning tree (802.1D): blocks ports that would make a loop |
| `no spanning-tree` | config | switches | Turn spanning tree off (and forget its settings) |
| `spanning-tree priority PRIORITY` | config | switches | Priority (default 32768) |
| `spanning-tree hello-time SECONDS` | config | switches | Seconds |
| `spanning-tree max-age SECONDS` | config | switches | Seconds |
| `spanning-tree forward-time SECONDS` | config | switches | Seconds |
| `spanning-tree bridge-address MAC` | config | switches | MAC address |
| `no spanning-tree priority` | config | switches | Default priority |
| `no spanning-tree hello-time` | config | switches | Default hello time |
| `no spanning-tree max-age` | config | switches | Default max age |
| `no spanning-tree forward-time` | config | switches | Default forward time |
| `no spanning-tree bridge-address` | config | switches | Default bridge address |
| `spanning-tree cost COST` | interface | switches | Cost |
| `spanning-tree port-priority PRIORITY` | interface | switches | Priority (default 128) |
| `no spanning-tree cost` | interface | switches | Default cost |
| `no spanning-tree port-priority` | interface | switches | Default port priority |

### Services

What an IP device serves: DNS names, DHCP pools, DHCP relay, TCP echo.

| Command | Mode | Devices | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip dns server` | config | routers, hosts, servers | Answer DNS questions for the names set with ip host |
| `no ip dns server` | config | routers, hosts, servers | Stop answering DNS questions (and forget the names) |
| `ip host NAME ADDRESS` | config | routers, hosts, servers | Its IPv4 address |
| `no ip host NAME` | config | routers, hosts, servers | Forget a name |
| `ip dhcp pool NAME` | config | routers, hosts, servers | Pool name |
| `no ip dhcp pool NAME` | config | routers, hosts, servers | Delete a pool |
| `range FIRST LAST` | DHCP pool | all devices | Last address |
| `netmask MASK` | DHCP pool | all devices | Network mask |
| `default-router ADDRESS` | DHCP pool | all devices | Router address |
| `dns-server ADDRESS` | DHCP pool | all devices | DNS server address |
| `lease SECONDS` | DHCP pool | all devices | Seconds (default 3600) |
| `no netmask` | DHCP pool | all devices | Remove the mask |
| `no default-router` | DHCP pool | all devices | Tell clients no gateway |
| `no dns-server` | DHCP pool | all devices | Tell clients no DNS server |
| `no lease` | DHCP pool | all devices | Default lease time |
| `ip helper-address ADDRESS` | interface | routers | DHCP server address |
| `no ip helper-address` | interface | routers | Stop relaying DHCP on this interface |
| `no ip helper-address ADDRESS` | interface | routers | DHCP server address |
| `service tcp-echo PORT` | config | routers, hosts, servers | TCP port |
| `no service tcp-echo PORT` | config | routers, hosts, servers | Stop the TCP echo service on a port |

### Rip

RIPv2 in FRRouting's style: router rip, then network, passive-interface and timers basic. Split horizon and triggered updates are per router here (FRR sets them per interface).

| Command | Mode | Devices | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `router rip` | config | routers | Routing Information Protocol (version 2) |
| `no router rip` | config | routers | Turn RIP off |
| `version 2` | routing | routers | RIPv2 (the only version) |
| `network PREFIX` | routing | routers | Network and prefix length |
| `network IFNAME` | routing | routers | Run RIP on this interface |
| `no network PREFIX` | routing | routers | Network and prefix length |
| `no network IFNAME` | routing | routers | Interface name |
| `passive-interface IFNAME` | routing | routers | Interface name |
| `no passive-interface IFNAME` | routing | routers | Interface name |
| `timers basic UPDATE TIMEOUT GARBAGE` | routing | routers | Seconds an invalid route is kept (default 120) |
| `no timers basic` | routing | routers | Back to the default timers |
| `split-horizon simple` | routing | routers | Leave them out (the default) |
| `split-horizon poisoned-reverse` | routing | routers | Advertise them with metric 16 |
| `no split-horizon` | routing | routers | Advertise everything everywhere |
| `triggered-updates` | routing | routers | Send changes at once (the default) |
| `no triggered-updates` | routing | routers | Wait for the update timer (a teaching setting, not in FRR) |

### Show

Show commands. Every one also takes | json, | include WORD and | exclude WORD.

| Command | Mode | Devices | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `show running-config` | privileged | all devices | The configuration, as commands that rebuild it |
| `show running-config openconfig` | privileged | all devices | The configuration in OpenConfig's JSON form |
| `show version` | user, privileged | all devices | Software, device kind and backend |
| `show interfaces` | user, privileged | all devices | Details of every interface: state, MAC, addresses, VLANs, shaping |
| `show interfaces IFNAME` | user, privileged | all devices | The interface to describe |
| `show interface brief` | user, privileged | all devices | One line per interface |
| `show ip interface brief` | user, privileged | all devices | One line per interface |
| `show ip route` | user, privileged | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Routing table: where each network is sent |
| `show arp` | user, privileged | routers, hosts, servers, switches | IPv4 address to MAC address table |
| `show ip dhcp binding` | user, privileged | routers, hosts, servers | Addresses this server has handed out |
| `show mac address-table` | user, privileged | switches | Which port each MAC address was seen on |
| `show spanning-tree` | user, privileged | switches | Root bridge, port roles and states |
| `show vlan brief` | user, privileged | switches | VLANs with their access ports, and the trunks |
| `show vlan` | user, privileged | switches | VLANs |

### Exec

Commands that run something on the device now (ping, traceroute) instead of reading or changing configuration. Each takes | json like a show command.

| Command | Mode | Devices | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ping ADDRESS` | user, privileged | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Address to ping |
| `traceroute ADDRESS` | user, privileged | routers, hosts, servers, switches | Destination address |

## Examples

### Look at a router: addresses, routes, neighbours, `| json`

Lab `routed-lan-dns`, device `R1`:

```text
R1>enable
R1#show version
OpenPacketRouter CLI (Apache-2.0)
Device R1, a router, running on the engine backend
R1#show ip interface brief
Interface  Address      Method  Admin  Link
eth0       10.0.0.1/24  manual  up     up
eth1       10.1.0.1/24  manual  up     up
R1#ping 10.1.0.53
Reply from 10.1.0.53: time 8 ms
ping 10.1.0.53: 1 sent, 1 answered
R1#show arp
Address    MAC                Interface
10.1.0.53  02:00:00:00:00:04  eth1
R1#show arp | json
[
  {
    "ip": "10.1.0.53",
    "mac": "02:00:00:00:00:04",
    "interface": "eth1"
  }
]
R1#traceroute 10.1.0.53
Route to 10.1.0.53:
  1  10.1.0.53
```

Shapes of the `| json` output of each show command:

| Command | JSON |
|---|---|
| `show ip interface brief` (also `show interface brief`) | a list: `name`, `address`, `method` (`manual` or `dhcp`), `admin` (`up` or `down`), `link` |
| `show ip route` | a list: `prefix`, `protocol` (`connected` or `static`), `nextHop` (static only), `interface` |
| `show arp` | a list: `ip`, `mac`, `interface` |
| `show ip dhcp binding` | a list: `ip`, `mac` |
| `show mac address-table` | a list: `vlan`, `mac`, `port` |
| `show vlan brief` | an object: `vlans` (`vlan`, `name`, `accessPorts`) and `trunks` (`port`, `allowed`, `native`) |
| `show spanning-tree` | an object: `bridgeId`, `root`, `isRoot`, `rootCost`, `rootPort`, and `ports` (each port: `role`, `state`, `cost`, …) |
| `show running-config openconfig` | the configuration in the standard OpenConfig JSON layout |

A list that is empty (`[]`) means the device has not learned anything yet. ARP, MAC and DHCP tables fill up as
traffic flows, so run a `ping` first.

### Change a router: add a route

Lab `routed-lan-dns`, device `R1`:

```text
R1>enable
R1#configure terminal
Configuring from the terminal. Type end or press Ctrl-Z to finish.
R1(config)#ip route 10.9.0.0/16 10.1.0.53
R1(config)#end
R1#show ip route
Legend: C = connected network, S = static route

C  10.0.0.0/24 on eth0 (directly connected)
C  10.1.0.0/24 on eth1 (directly connected)
S  10.9.0.0/16 via 10.1.0.53, out eth1
R1#show running-config
hostname R1
!
interface eth0
 ip address 10.0.0.1/24
!
interface eth1
 ip address 10.1.0.1/24
!
ip route 10.9.0.0/16 10.1.0.53
!
end
```

### Set up a switch: VLANs on ports

Lab `vlans`, device `SW1`:

```text
SW1>enable
SW1#show vlan brief
VLAN  Name      Access ports
10    VLAN0010  p1
20    VLAN0020  p2

Trunk  Allowed VLANs  Native
trunk  10,20          1
SW1#configure terminal
Configuring from the terminal. Type end or press Ctrl-Z to finish.
SW1(config)#interface p1
SW1(config-if)#switchport access vlan 20
SW1(config-if)#end
SW1#show vlan brief
VLAN  Name      Access ports
10    VLAN0010  -
20    VLAN0020  p1, p2

Trunk  Allowed VLANs  Native
trunk  10,20          1
SW1#show vlan brief | json
{
  "vlans": [
    {
      "vlan": 10,
      "name": "VLAN0010",
      "accessPorts": []
    },
    {
      "vlan": 20,
      "name": "VLAN0020",
      "accessPorts": [
        "p1",
        "p2"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "trunks": [
    {
      "port": "trunk",
      "allowed": [
        10,
        20
      ],
      "native": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

### Spanning tree: who is the root?

Lab `loop-with-stp`, device `SW1`:

```text
SW1>enable
SW1#show spanning-tree
Bridge 8000.02aa00000001  (this switch is the root)
Root   8000.02aa00000001

Port  Role        State       Cost  Port ID
p1    designated  forwarding  19    128.1
p2    designated  forwarding  19    128.2
p3    designated  forwarding  19    128.3
SW1#configure terminal
Configuring from the terminal. Type end or press Ctrl-Z to finish.
SW1(config)#spanning-tree priority 61440
SW1(config)#end
SW1#show spanning-tree | include Bridge
Bridge f000.02aa00000001
```

### DHCP: a server with an address pool

Lab `dhcp-router`, device `DHCP`:

```text
DHCP>enable
DHCP#show running-config
hostname DHCP
!
interface eth0
 ip address 10.0.0.2/24
!
ip route 0.0.0.0/0 10.0.0.1
!

!
end
DHCP#show ip dhcp binding | json
[]
```

### Refused commands

Lab `routed-lan-dns`, device `R1`:

```text
R1>enable
R1#configure terminal
Configuring from the terminal. Type end or press Ctrl-Z to finish.
R1(config)#ip route 10.9.0.0/16 192.168.77.1
% node "R1": next hop 192.168.77.1 is not on any of its subnets
R1(config)#hostname bad name
                        ^
% Unknown word at '^'
R1(config)#show ip route
           ^
% Unknown word at '^'
```

## One configuration, other systems

`--render` prints the same configuration as commands for a real system, so a lab can be copied to real gear:

```bash
node cli/bin/opr-cli.mjs examples/routed-lan-dns/spec.json R1 --render linux     # iproute2 commands
node cli/bin/opr-cli.mjs examples/routed-lan-dns/spec.json R1 --render frr       # FRRouting config
node cli/bin/opr-cli.mjs examples/routed-lan-dns/spec.json R1 --render openwrt   # OpenWrt UCI commands
```

For Linux, add `--lab-parity` to include the extra settings that make the real kernel's frames match the engine's, as the validators use.
